title: Marion County School District Referendum: Renew the One-Mill Levy
what_it_does: School-district ballot question (Yes / No). Passes with a simple majority of votes cast on the question.
ballot_summary: Marion County voters will decide whether to renew the school district's one-mill operating levy for four more years, July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2031, for safe schools, reading, physical education, art, music, early learning, library/media and vocational programs, class-size requirements and retaining certified teachers, with an independent citizens' oversight committee. Voters first approved the levy in 2014 and renewed it in 2018 and 2022.
what_yes_means: A YES vote continues the one-mill levy, which raises about $41 million a year, through June 2031.
what_no_means: A NO vote lets it expire June 30, 2027.
verified_ballot_note: Summary from Marion County Public Schools' Funding Referendum Oversight Committee page (https://www.marionschools.net/school_board/funding_referendum_oversight_committee) and Ballotpedia's measure page (https://ballotpedia.org/Marion_County_One_Mill_School_Funding_Referendum). Exact 2026 ballot wording to be confirmed on the Marion sample ballot.
